Start here

Where the code lives and what to edit for a change: docs/MAP.md, one page. The pipeline in one picture: docs/OVERVIEW.md. Routine operation: docs/OPERATIONS.md.

For an operator or an automated agent taking over a fresh clone. Read this, then git log for recent changes, then the document for the area being changed.

What this is, in four sentences

A pipeline reads a company's SEC 10-K filings and returns revenue, capex and opex, each citing the exact table cell it came from, checked against the SEC's own XBRL data and re-read on the rendered filing. A second set of agents reads the notes, the MD&A, earnings releases and call transcripts for facts and statements about AI. An attributor reads a money-flow model for the company's industry and the cleaned data and says how much of the capex is AI, naming every input so code recomputes the number. A person edits the models and definitions, reruns, checks against a reference set, and signs a release; nobody is asked anything else.

Built by Kenny Geiler in October 2026 as a working prototype for Arctal. 100 companies across the AI supply chain (docs/COMPANIES.md), annual, fiscal years 2022 to 2026. See docs/PROOF.md for who Arctal is and why the app looks the way it does.

What a clone contains, and what it does not

Tracked, present on clone:

Code (ledger/), tests (tests/), the rules (rules/*.yaml), the agents' prompts (agents/), the taxonomy (taxonomy/: the categories and their standards, the asset-type mappings, the stated figures), per-company definitions (definitions/companies.yaml), the investor-page links (sources/ir.yaml), the hand-check (golden/), the golden test's frozen inputs and expectation (fixtures/), the gold set a person verifies (gold/, T82, docs/EVALS.md).
Every agent output, kept as evidence: data/extract/outputs/ (statement cells), data/notes/outputs/ (note facts), data/aispend/outputs/ (AI statements), data/projects/outputs/ (named projects). A rebuild reuses them; no agent runs unless a task changes.
Signed releases (releases/v*/), the decisions log (decisions/), the reports and evidence screenshots (reports/), and every document in docs/.

Not tracked, rebuilt by ledger run (needs the network and about 30 minutes for all 31):

The database data/ledger.duckdb, the raw filings data/raw/, parsed tables data/docs/, MD&A and release texts data/text/, the task files, snapshots, data/watch.json, the jobs folder, resolutions.jsonl, dry runs.
Setup
uv sync                                                     # Python 3.12, DuckDB, edgartools, pypdf, playwright
echo 'SEC_USER_AGENT="Your Name you@example.com"' > .env     # the SEC requires a contact; never commit it
echo 'DATABASE_URL="postgresql://…"' >> .env                 # production Postgres, only to publish releases
echo 'DATABASE_READONLY_URL="postgresql://…"' >> .env        # the arctal_reader string, SELECT only; the one to hand a consumer
claude                                                      # then /login: the agents run on a Claude subscription, headless
export LEDGER_CLAUDE="$(which claude)"                      # the claude binary the pipeline should use
uv run python -m ledger test --fast                         # the whole suite, offline, a few minutes; the count and result land in reports/tests.json (drop --fast for golden too)

Offline mode (LEDGER_OFFLINE=1, ledger/ingest/edgar.py): every SEC read is served from the data/raw cache whatever its age (under a temporary LEDGER_ROOT, from the checkout's own data/raw), and anything uncached raises Offline; the edgartools and investor-PDF paths refuse too. No SEC_USER_AGENT is needed. ledger test and ledger golden --check run offline unless --online, and tests/__init__.py sets it for a bare python -m unittest, so a worktree with no .env runs the whole suite. A test that needs a filing must find it in data/raw (symlinked in a worktree) or fail with Offline.

The evidence step drives the installed Google Chrome through Playwright. The texts step downloads PDFs from the links in sources/ir.yaml; it never renders investor pages (they sit behind a bot check, and code must not get around it; a person lists the links).

The five-minute tour
uv run python -m ledger run --ticker NVDA        # every step for one company, agents included, then the scorecard
uv run python -m ledger run --stage 3            # all 31 (about 30 minutes on a fresh clone, mostly fetching and Chrome)
uv run python -m ledger app                      # Kenny's Data Emporium at http://127.0.0.1:3610 (LEDGER_CLAUDE="$(which claude)" only to start runs from it)
uv run python -m ledger golden --check           # the proven six rebuilt from frozen inputs, every table compared, plus every gold verdict
uv run python -m ledger gold --status            # the gold set: verdicts, error rate with n and a Wilson interval (--draw writes the sample)
uv run python -m ledger test                     # the whole suite, golden included; writes reports/tests.json, the Release page's test line (--fast skips golden)
uv run python -m ledger mapper MU                # the mapping assistant (T33): a us-gaap member proposed per unmapped PP&E category; approve on #reconcile?scope=MU
uv run python -m ledger release v1.8.0           # the scope (config.SCOPE), a gate table per company; refuses on any failing row; then signoff, by the owner only
uv run python -m ledger publish v1.5.0           # a signed release to the production Postgres; --status lists what is there

Every command takes --stage 3 (every tracked company) or --ticker X Y. python -m ledger lists them.

The objects, and where each lives
OBJECT	WHAT IT IS	FILE OR TABLE	DOC
values	revenue, capex, opex per company and fiscal year, f

Map: where is X

A map, not a manual. Tables are DuckDB (ledger/core/store.py declares them); files are tracked unless marked. The state machines are ledger/core/states.py (docs/STATES.md). Commands are uv run python -m ledger <command>, one module each in ledger/cli/ (they do the table writes: store.write).

Packages
PACKAGE	JOB	WRITES	READS
ledger/core/	the store, config, the state machines, the one definition of open	the schema	everything
ledger/ingest/	fetch and parse filings; texts; the XBRL answer key (reference/)	documents, reference_values, texts; data/raw, data/docs, data/text (untracked)	the SEC (or data/raw offline)
ledger/extract/	the agents: tasks, headless runs, output contracts, loaders	extractions, note_extractions, facts, ai_statements, ai_spend, projects, runs; data/*/outputs/	documents, texts
ledger/checks/	everything that checks a number: reconcile labels, rules, ties, crops, faults, Proof, golden	values, exceptions, rules; reports/evidence/crops.json	the extracted tables
ledger/review/	what a person decides: resolutions, decisions, mappings, definitions, gold verdicts, Reconcile	decisions/*.jsonl, taxonomy/asset_types.yaml, definitions/companies.yaml, rules/*.yaml (explains rules), gold/*.json	the checks
ledger/release/	what ships: the taxonomy rows, the checklist, the packet, signing, publishing, the claims register	releases/v*/, Postgres, reports/tests.json, docs/CLAIMS.md, claims/hosted.json	everything above
ledger/web/	Kenny's Data Emporium (port 3610): routes, the read API, trail cards, the filing viewer, pages	data/views.json	everything above
Key modules
MODULE	OWNS	STATE MACHINE IT DECIDES
core/status.py	the one definition of open: checked / explained / open / blocked (_state, of_value, of_fact, of_mapping)	row groups (M1)
core/states.py	every state that reaches a page: its states, moves, deciding function, page word; /pages/_states.js, /api/v1/states	all ten: row, ladder, check, mapping, crop, gold, gold_group, crosscheck, line, edgar
core/store.py	DuckDB schema, write contracts, data/ledger.duckdb, docs/DATA_DICTIONARY.md	
core/config.py	companies, years, fields, PROVEN, SCOPE, PEOPLE, INDUSTRIES	
ingest/edgar.py	the SEC client, its cache, LEDGER_OFFLINE	
ingest/tables.py, statements.py	the table parser, the statement locator	
extract/extract.py, notes.py, guidance.py, projects.py	task packing, output contract and loader per reader (statements, notes, AI statements, projects)	
extract/agent.py, agents.py	the headless claude -p run; the named agents (agents/agents.json)	
checks/reconcile.py	fiscal-year values and their label against XBRL	check (M1a)
checks/rules.py, guards.py	the rule engine over rules/*.yaml; the part-year and program guards	
checks/ties.py	readings across filings and ties to totals: the note-figure ladder (fact_state)	ladder (M1b)
checks/crops.py	a picture of every cited cell, reports/evidence/crops.json	crop (M14)
checks/calc.py	a figure calculated from several cells: formula, arithmetic, roles, cross-checks (filing total, XBRL)	crosscheck (M18)
checks/proof.py	Proof: every row's state per stage per company	
checks/golden.py	the golden test (fixtures/)	
review/resolutions.py	decisions/resolutions.jsonl, keys (key_for)	
review/workbench.py	Reconcile's rows	
review/mapper.py, mapcard.py	the mapping assistant and the mapping decision card	mapping (M5, via status.of_mapping)
review/gold.py	the gold set, verdicts, error rate per group, hard items first	gold (M7), gold_group (M17)
release/taxonomy.py	the taxonomy rows (/api/v1/taxonomy, taxonomy.csv)	
release/checklist.py	the Release page's checklist and the Sign act	line (M9)
release/claims.py	the claims register, the page scan, docs/CLAIMS.md	
web/app.py	every route; pages/*.js and app.html	
web/docs.py	the Docs section: top-level docs/*.md served read-only, the glossary and the rules page written from code	
web/cards.py	the trail's evidence cards and status tiles	edgar freshness via states.edgar (M12)
To change X, edit Y
TO CHANGE	EDIT	THEN
notes extraction logic	ledger/extract/notes.py (contract, loader); the prompt is a new version in agents/prompts/ (never in place)	ledger notes --run then --load; golden --check
a rule	rules/<id>.yaml; a new check function in ledger/checks/rules.py	ledger rules; golden --check
a company-specific definition	definitions/companies.yaml (who, why, periods), or "Make this a definition" on Reconcile	ledger reconcile, ledger rules
a category mapping	Reconcile's asset types group (writes taxonomy/asset_types.yaml confirmed), or ledger mapper <T> for proposals	any taxonomy read
UI copy, a state's label	a state word: ledger/core/states.py only; other copy: ledger/web/pages/<page>.js or web/cards.py; register every shown string in claims/claims.yaml	ledger claims; tests.test_states, tests.test_claims
a new state	declare it in ledger/core/states.py (kind, word, moves), return it from the machine's deciding function	tests/test_states.py
adding a company	ledger run --ticker X; its industry in ledger/core/config.py INDUSTRIES	docs/COMPANIES.md
crops	ledger/checks/crops.py; pictures are untracked	ledger evidence --crops --ticker …
the release gate	ledger/release/checklist.py (lines), ledger/release/release.py (GATES: G1, G4, G5, G6)	tests/test_checklist.py
Naming
Finding ids (claims/findings.jsonl, append-only, union-merged): F-<BRANCH CODE><n> (F-RC7), or S-<n> for a state finding; plain F<n> stops at F30. Close one by appending a line with the same id, new status and at.
Prompt versions: <agent>@v<n> (notes@v3); a change is the next version, switched on as a second step.
Change records: the commit message (what, why, what is left open); there is no status diary. docs/CLAIMS.md is generated: ledger c

Operating guide

The routine work of running the ledger: the daily review, grading the gold set, adding a company, cutting a release, and what to do when a Release line is red. Setup and the objects are in Handoff; what each word means is in the Glossary. Commands are uv run python -m ledger <command>, shortened here to ledger <command>.

Never
Never sign a release that was not reviewed. Signing is the one human act and belongs to the owner. Agents never sign or publish.
Never run the agents on the paid API. They run headless on a Claude subscription through claude -p (LEDGER_CLAUDE).
Never edit a prompt or the taxonomy in place. A prompt change is the next version in agents/prompts/ (<agent>@v<n>), switched on in agents/agents.json as a second step. A taxonomy or mapping change goes through Reconcile or a reviewed commit.
Never ingest in a worktree. Worktrees share data/raw, data/docs and data/text with the main checkout; an ingest on an older base rewrites the shared parses with old code. Run ingest only on current main.
Never freeze golden by accident. ledger golden --freeze only on purpose, in its own commit that says why.
Never edit a file under releases/, decisions/ or the agents' history. They are append-only or hashed.
Never commit .env. The SEC contact and the database URLs live only there.
Never get around a bot check. Investor-page links are listed by a person in sources/ir.yaml.
Daily review
ledger watch asks EDGAR for 10-Ks and 10-K/As the ledger has not read; ledger watch --run reads them. The company trail shows the age of the last check ("SEC checked", or "out of date" after 48 hours).
Open Proof. Each company in scope shows its rows by state per stage. A company is proven when nothing is open.
Open Reconcile. Every item is open or blocked, with the evidence and the reason code could not decide it. For each:
Accept or Explain when the figure is right and the reason is specific to this item.
Make this a rule or Make this a definition when the same reason will recur: the explanation is written once (rules/ or definitions/companies.yaml) and applies on every run.
Fix when the figure is wrong: the item stays open until the pipeline produces the right one.
Block release when the figure must not ship.
For an asset-type proposal: Approve, Edit or Reject. Only an approval writes confirmed_by.
After a definition or rule, run ledger rules (or ledger reconcile), then commit the changed file. The commit message says what was decided and why.
A new kind of failure gets a row in docs/INGESTION.md and taxonomy/failures.yaml, a check that catches it, and a test.

The name in the signer box is the author of every decision. It must be on config.PEOPLE; there is no sign-in yet, so the name is a claim, not proof of a person.

Grading the gold set

The gold set (gold/<TICKER>.json, the Hand check on Proof) is about 10 values and 10 facts per proven company, stratified by field and year, untagged facts oversampled.

On Proof, the Hand check section lists the gold items per company. Each item shows the claim, the cited cells and their crops.
Open the filing at the cell and give a verdict: Right (the filing shows this number here), Wrong (it shows something else) or Can't say (the filing does not settle it), with a note.
ledger gold --status prints the verdicts and the error rate: wrong of (right + wrong), with n and a Wilson 95% interval. Can't say is counted beside it.
ledger golden --check compares every verdict with the current tables. A Right item whose value changed fails as "changed since verdict, re-verify".
Each new release version draws a new sample: ledger gold --draw. Items with a verdict are never overwritten or dropped.
Adding a company
ledger run --ticker X runs every step for it, agents included (network and LEDGER_CLAUDE required). It joins stage 3, not the release scope.
Give it an industry in ledger/core/config.py INDUSTRIES and a line in docs/COMPANIES.md.
Map its PP&E categories: ledger mapper X, then approve on #reconcile?scope=X.
Review its open items on Reconcile. It enters the proven set (config.PROVEN) only when nothing is open, and then the golden fixtures are frozen again on purpose.
Cutting a release

After any merge, in this order, committing after each:

ledger golden --check (rewrites reports/golden.json).
ledger claims (regenerates docs/CLAIMS.md).
ledger test on that commit (rewrites reports/tests.json).

Then open Release. The checklist builds the packet in memory and shows every line that could make a signature wrong. When every required line is green, the Sign button writes releases/<version>/, signs as the name in the signer box, stores the checklist in SIGNOFF.json and publishes. From the command line: ledger release vX.Y.Z builds and prints the gate table, ledger signoff vX.Y.Z --by "<name>" signs, ledger publish vX.Y.Z pushes a signed release to Postgres.

When a Release line is red
LINE	MEANING	WHAT TO DO
All filings read (G1)	A filing ended in a failure that is still open	On Proof, find the failed step; rerun it (--run, then --load) or log the failure type
Every block has a decision (G4)	A block-severity rule fired with no current decision	Decide each item on Reconcile
Values confirmed on filing (G5)	A value XBRL cannot vouch for was not confirmed on the rendered filing	ledger evidence --ticker X; where the re-read cannot confirm, a person confirms in the hand-check file
Proposed (G6)	A run's decision or an asset-type mapping has no person's confirmation; the same count as Reconcile's Proposed	Reconcile, "to confirm" and "asset types" groups
Needs review	Rows neither checked nor explained, nothing proposed (an unmapped asset type is one); the same count as Reconcile's Needs review	R

Glossary

Written from code on every request: the state words from ledger/core/states.py, the terms from ledger/web/docs.py. A state word belongs to exactly one state machine (or names one group of its states); States describes each machine.

State words
WORD	MACHINE	STATE	KIND	MEANING
Verified	row (M1)	ok	good	checked by an SEC XBRL match or a quote that matches its source
Corroborated	row (M1)	corroborated	good	checked by a tie to the filing's tagged total, a second filing, or another answer key
Matches company tag	row (M1)	company	good	a category the company's own XBRL tag matches
Done	row (M1)	done	neutral	found or confirmed, not checked: statements located, no blocking items, a person's confirmation
Unverified	row (M1)	info	neutral	explained: a citation only, a definition, a decision, an info rule
Proposed	row (M1)	wait	open	a proposal no person has confirmed (a mapping, a run's decision)
Needs review	row (M1)	bad	open	open: neither checked nor explained
Blocks release	row (M1)	blocked	bad	a block rule fired or a person's decision blocks
Not checked	row (M1)	unknown	unknown	no state was computed for the row
Checked	row (M1)	group checked	group	ok, corroborated, company
Located/Done	row (M1)	group done	group	done
Unverified	row (M1)	group explained	group	info
To review	row (M1)	group open	group	wait, bad
Blocks release	row (M1)	group blocked	group	blocked
Verified	ladder (M1b)	xbrl	good	the filing's XBRL tags the same value
Matches company tag	ladder (M1b)	filer_tag	good	the company's own tag on the category
Corroborated	ladder (M1b)	tie	good	the parts tie to the total the same filing tags
Corroborated	ladder (M1b)	reading	good	a second filing prints the same figure
Corroborated	ladder (M1b)	keyed	good	another answer key agreed
Unverified	ladder (M1b)	citation_only	neutral	untagged, no tie, one reading: the citation is all
Unverified	ladder (M1b)	explained	neutral	a decision, a definition or a guard explains it
Needs review	ladder (M1b)	readings_differ	open	two filings print different figures
Needs review	ladder (M1b)	differs	open	the cell differs from its tag, or nothing explains it
Not checked	ladder (M1b)	not_looked_up	unknown	the instance was never loaded: not produced yet, it reads citation_only (F17)
Verified	check (M1a)	agree	good	the cell agrees with the SEC's XBRL value
Differs from SEC XBRL	check (M1a)	unresolved	open	the cell differs from the SEC's XBRL value
Unverified · definition	check (M1a)	definition_gap	neutral	differs, and a definition on file says why
Unverified · citation only	check (M1a)	no_reference	neutral	no XBRL value to compare
Not reported	check (M1a)	not_reported	neutral	the company reports no such line and XBRL has none
In SEC XBRL, not extracted	check (M1a)	not_extracted	open	XBRL holds a value the reader did not extract (T65)
Not checked	check (M1a)	unknown	unknown	no label: the row was not reconciled
Done	mapping (M5)	confirmed	neutral	a person confirmed the member (confirmed_by)
Matches company tag	mapping (M5)	filer_tag	good	the company's own XBRL tags the category with the proposed member
Proposed	mapping (M5)	to_confirm	open	an entry no person confirmed (T63)
Unmapped	mapping (M5)	unmapped	open	no entry in taxonomy/asset_types.yaml (the trail says the row's word, Needs review)
Cell located	crop (M14)	located	good	the locator found the cited text; the picture is the one written
Cell not located	crop (M14)	not_located	bad	the locator did not find the cited text there
Crop out of date	crop (M14)	stale	stale	the filing, its fingerprint, the citation or the crop code changed since
Crop file missing	crop (M14)	missing	missing	the picture is gone or not the one written
No crop	crop (M14)	none	unknown	no crop on record, or no extraction on file
Unchecked	gold (M7)	unchecked	unknown	no verdict yet: never a pass
Right	gold (M7)	right	good	the filing shows this number at this cell
Wrong	gold (M7)	wrong	bad	the filing shows something else
Can’t say	gold (M7)	cant_say	neutral	the filing does not settle it
No SEC counterpart	gold_group (M17)	no_counterpart	neutral	no XBRL value to compare (no_reference, not_reported): the person is the only check
Definition differs	gold_group (M17)	definition	neutral	an XBRL value exists and differs (definition_gap, unresolved)
Not extracted	gold_group (M17)	not_extracted	open	XBRL holds a value the reader did not extract (not_extracted)
Not reconciled	gold_group (M17)	not_reconciled	unknown	no label, or a label off the list: the row was never compared
Calculated	gold_group (M17)	calculated	good	agrees with SEC XBRL, and its calculation from several cells holds (calc.holds)
Matches SEC XBRL	gold_group (M17)	xbrl	good	agrees with SEC XBRL: already machine-checked
matches	crosscheck (M18)	matches	good	the filing's own total, or SEC XBRL, equals the calculation within rounding
includes	crosscheck (M18)	explained	neutral	the filing's own total differs by exactly one formula input, sign-aware, and by no other line (a wider measure: Amazon's total includes cost of sales)
differs by	crosscheck (M18)	differs	open	the other total differs; the page names the line of that amount only when exactly one line is
No total to compare	crosscheck (M18)	none	unknown	the filing prints no such total in that column, or XBRL has no value
Pass	line (M9)	pass	good	—
Fail	line (M9)	fail	bad	—
Info	line (M9)	info	neutral	informs, never blocks
Not run	line (M9)	not_run	unknown	the input the line reads does not exist
Stale	line (M9)	stale	stale	the input exists but is from other code (another commit, a dirty tree)
SEC checked	edgar (M12)	fresh	good	checked within 48 hours; the page adds the age
out of date	edgar (M12)	stale	stale	older than 48 hours; the page adds the age
SEC never check

Rules and checks

Written from code on every request: rules/*.yaml, ledger/core/status.py (answer keys) and ledger/release/release.py (gates). Every check is deterministic code; no model grades another model.

Order of checks
The task hides the answer key: the reader sees the statement tables, never an XBRL value or tag (ledger/extract/extract.py).
Shape: the answer must match its JSON schema (agents/schemas/); one retry with the reason, then a logged failure.
Citation: every value's cell must exist in the parsed filing and equal the value (citation_resolves).
Rules: 8 block, 10 warn, 3 info (21 in rules/).
Answer keys: the strongest key that agrees decides the row's word (below).
A second read on the rendered 10-K: the cited cell located by row label and column header, cropped and boxed (ledger/checks/crops.py).
Answer keys, strongest first
KEY	BY PREFIXES	WHY IT RANKS HERE
twin	xbrl, esef	a separate preparer's machine-readable instance: the filer tagged the number for a different reader, by a different process, from the text the pipeline read
second source	source	the same issuer's other document: the same finance team wrote both, so an error upstream of both documents is shared
tie	rule	arithmetic inside the same document: the parts and the whole agree, which shows consistent reading, not a right number
later truth	actual	a later period's actual against the plan: the actual can itself be restated, and it proves the plan, not the reading
second reading	reading	the same filer's next 10-K printing the same figure: usually the table carried forward by the same preparer and read by the same reader, so it rules out a one-off misread, nothing upstream
Rules

Block refuses the release until decided; warn opens the rows it fires on; info explains.

Each rule's rationale and owner are in its file; the file's hash is recorded in every release manifest.

RULE	SEVERITY	CHECK	WHAT IT CHECKS	FILE
citation_resolves	block	citation_resolves	Every agent value cites a table, row, column and cell that exist in the parsed filing, and the cell × unit (with the field's sign rule) equals the value.	rules/citation_resolves.yaml
column_matches_period	block	column_matches_period	The cited column's label agrees with the period the value claims (end date or year, and length).	rules/column_matches_period.yaml
cost_lines_summed	block	cost_lines_summed	When a company reports no total cost-of-revenue line, the cost lines an agent classified as cost of revenue were added up; the rule lists them.	rules/cost_lines_summed.yaml
period_length	block	period_length	Each value read from a 10-K covers one fiscal year.	rules/period_length.yaml
sign	block	sign	Revenue, capex and opex are never negative.	rules/sign.yaml
